[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1997|4|10|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Koper]], Slovenia | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 8 | weight_lbs = 236 | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 49 | draft_team = [[Denver Nuggets]] | career_start = 2014 | career_end = | years1 = 2014–2016 | team1 = [[KK Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] | years2 = 2014–2016 | team2 = →[[KK Škofja Loka|LTH Castings]] | years3 = 2016–2018 | team3 = [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] | years4 = 2018 | team4 = →[[CB San Pablo Burgos|San Pablo Burgos]] | years5 = 2018–2019 | team5 = San Pablo Burgos | years6 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team6 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years7 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019]] | team7 = →[[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]] | years8 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]] | team8 = →[[Grand Rapids Gold]] | years9 = 2025 | team9 = [[Olimpia Milano]] | years10 = 2026–present | team10 = San Pablo Burgos | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]) * [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]] ([[2018–19 ACB season|2019]]) * [[Italian Basketball Supercup|Italian Supercup]] winner (2025) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|SLO}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[EuroBasket]]}} {{MedalGold|[[EuroBasket 2017|2017 Finland–Israel–Romania–Turkey]]|}} }} '''Vlatko Čančar''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|tʃ|ɑː|n|tʃ|ɑr}} {{respell|CHAHN|char}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=24 October 2023|access-date=17 May 2024}} born 10 April 1997) is a Slovenian professional [[basketball]] player for [[CB San Pablo Burgos|San Pablo Burgos]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=8}}, he plays primarily as a [[small forward]]. He has previously played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Denver Nuggets]], winning the [[NBA Finals]] with them in [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. ==Professional career== ===Union Olimpija (2015–2016)=== On 16 April 2015, Čančar signed a five-year contract with [[KK Olimpija|Union Olimpija]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/slovenia/158538/olimpija-ljubljana-signs-vlatko-cancar-to-a-5-year-contract.html |title=Olimpija Ljubljana signs Vlatko Cancar to a 5-year contract |work=Sportando |date=16 April 2017 |access-date=12 July 2017 |archive-date=12 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712120935/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/slovenia/158538/olimpija-ljubljana-signs-vlatko-cancar-to-a-5-year-contract.html}} ===Mega Leks (2016–2018)=== On 30 June 2016, Čančar left Olimpija and signed with Serbian team [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]].{{cite news |title=Čančar from Union Olimpija to Mega Leks |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/36650/cancar-from-union-olimpija-to-mega-leks/ |access-date=27 September 2023 |date=30 June 2016 |language=en}} ===San Pablo Burgos (2018–2019)=== On 13 March 2018, Čančar was loaned to the Spanish club [[CB San Pablo Burgos|San Pablo Burgos]].{{cite news |title=Vlatko Čančar se seli v Burgos |url=https://stara.kzs.si/clanek/Vlatko-Cancar-se-seli-v-Burgos/id/756/fcid/31 |access-date=27 September 2023 |work=KZS |date=13 March 2018 |language=sl}} On 13 June 2018, Čančar renewed his contract with the club for an additional two seasons.{{cite news |title=ACB.COM - Vlatko Čančar renueva con el San Pablo Burgos por dos años |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=141429|access-date=2 August 2019 |work=ACB.com |date=13 June 2018 |language=es-ES |archive-date=27 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827050838/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=141429 |url-status=dead}} ===Denver Nuggets (2019–2025)=== On 22 June 2017, Čančar was selected with the 49th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=2017 NBA Draft|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2017.html|website=Basketball-Reference|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 2 August 2019, Čančar signed his rookie contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets sign Vlatko Čančar|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-vlatko-cancar-20190802|website=NBA.com|date=2 August 2019|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 13 May 2021, Čančar scored a career-high 14 points off the bench in a 114–103 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite news|title=Jokic scores 31 points; Nuggets beat Timberwolves 114-103|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/jokic-scores-31-points-nuggets-beat-timberwolves-114-103/|website=CBSSports.com|date=14 May 2021|access-date=27 September 2023|quote=JaVale McGee had 12 points and 13 rebounds, and Vlatko Cancar scored a career-high 14 points off the bench for Denver.}}{{cite web|title=Nikola Jokic leads super-sized Nuggets past Timberwolves|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2021/05/13/nikola-jokic-leads-nuggets-past-timberwolves/|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=13 May 2021|access-date=27 September 2023|quote=Both Markus Howard (15 points) and Vlatko Cancar (14) enjoyed career-highs and helped offset Karl-Anthony Towns’ 20-point, 11-rebound effort for Minnesota.}} On 3 January 2022, during a 89–103 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Čančar suffered a right foot injury. Two days later, he was diagnosed with a fracture of his right [[Fifth metatarsal bone|fifth metatarsal]].{{cite news|title=Vlatko Cancar out indefinitely due to fractured right foot|url=https://basketnews.com/news-163191-vlatko-cancar-out-indefinitely-due-to-fractured-right-foot.html|website=BasketNews.com|date=5 January 2022|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 7 January, Čančar underwent surgery for the fracture and was ruled out for at least three months.{{cite news|title=Vlatko Čančar Injury Update|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/vlatko-cancar-injury-update-010722|website=NBA.com|date=7 January 2022|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 10 April, in the regular season finale, Čančar returned to the Nuggets and played a season high 24 minutes in an overtime loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Čančar recorded 2 points, 8 rebounds, and 4 assists in his last regular season game.{{cite web|title=Vlatko Cancar, Denver Nuggets, SF - 2021-22 Game Log - NBA|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/players/2844695/vlatko-cancar/game-log/2021/|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 7 July 2022, Čančar re-signed with the Nuggets on a three-year deal.{{cite news|title=Vlatko Cancar signs three-year contract extension with Nuggets|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/07/07/vlatko-cancar-nuggets-contract-extension/|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=7 July 2022|access-date=27 September 2023}} On 23 November 2022, Čančar scored a career high 20 points, along with 4 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 blocks in an overtime win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite news|title=Nikola Jokic, Bruce Brown and Vlatko Cancar save Nuggets with gripping OT win vs. Thunder|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/11/23/nuggets-gripping-ot-win-thunder/|work=The Denver Post|date=23 November 2022|access-date=27 September 2023|quote=Cancar scored a career-high 20 points, with numerous instances of spectacular defense to stymie the Thunder.}}{{cite web|title=Vlatko Čančar 2022-23 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/cancavl01/gamelog/2023/|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=27 September 2023}} In June 2023, Čančar won his first [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] when the Nuggets defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2023 NBA Finals]]. During the season, he played in 60 games, almost 15 minutes per game, and scored approximately five points per game.{{cite news|title=For Čančar, NBA ring a dream come true|url=https://sloveniatimes.com/38922/for-cancar-nba-ring-a-dream-come-true|website=SloveniaTimes.com|date=28 June 2023|access-date=27 September 2023}} In the five-game NBA Finals, he played for 29 seconds.{{cite news|title=Vlatko Čančar z Denverjem do naslova lige NBA! (VIDEO)|trans-title=Vlatko Cancar and Denver to the NBA title (VIDEO)|url=https://sportklub.n1info.si/kosarka/liga-nba/vlatko-cancar-z-denverjem-do-naslova-lige-nba-video/|newspaper=Sportklub N1info|date=13 June 2023|language=sl}} On 9 July 2024, Čančar re-signed with the Nuggets.{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets resign Vlatko Čančar|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-resign-vlatko-cancar-2|website=NBA.com|date=9 July 2024|access-date=14 July 2024}} ===Olimpia Milano (2025)=== On July 17, 2025, Čančar signed with [[Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web | last=Guzman | first=Matt | title=Denver Nuggets NBA Champion Signs with Team Overseas | website=Denver Nuggets On SI | date=2025-07-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/onsi/news/denver-nuggets-nba-champion-signs-with-team-overseas-01k0cx2g03ak | access-date=2025-12-06}} On October 22, of the same year, Čančar and his team have a mutual agreement to terminate his contract. He only appeared in two EuroLeague games during the season, the result of a knee issue.{{cite web|last=Gillingham|first=Geoff|title=Vlatko Cancar, Milan part ways|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/vlatko-cancar-olimpia-milano-part-ways/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|access-date=22 October 2025|date=22 October 2025}} ===Return to San Pablo Burgos (2026–present)=== On 21 July 2026, Čančar returned to [[CB San Pablo Burgos|San Pablo Burgos]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{cite web|title=Burgos brings back forward Vlatko Cancar|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/burgos-brings-back-forward-vlatko-cancar/|publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]|access-date=21 July 2026|date=21 July 2026}} ==National team career== Čančar has been a member of the [[Slovenia national basketball team]]. He played with the team at [[EuroBasket 2017]], where he won the gold medal with his country. Čančar represented the Slovenian national basketball team at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, Japan. On 4 August 2023, during an [[exhibition game]] against [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]], Čančar suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] in his left knee.{{cite web|last=Singer|first=Mike |title=Nuggets forward Vlatko Cancar suffers left ACL tear, source says|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2023/08/05/nuggets-vlatko-cancar-left-acl-tear/|publisher=[[The Denver Post]]|access-date=25 August 2026|date=5 August 2023}}{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|title=Sources: Nuggets F Vlatko Cancar suffers torn ACL in left knee|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38139377/sources-nuggets-f-vlatko-cancar-suffers-torn-acl-left-knee|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=25 August 2026|date=5 August 2023}} On 17 August 2023, he underwent surgery to reconstruct the ACL, and was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite web|last=Petersen|first=Will|title=Vlatko Cancar undergoes ACL surgery and a long recovery looms|url=https://denversports.com/nba/denver-nuggets/vlatko-cancar-undergoes-acl-surgery-and-a-long-recovery-looms/2106908|publisher=Denver Sports|access-date=25 August 2026|date=17 August 2023}} He ultimately missed the entire [[2023–24 NBA season]].{{cite web|last=Brooks|first=Matt|title=2024 Free Agency Profile: Vlatko Čančar|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/2024-free-agency-profile-vlatko-cancar|publisher=[[NBA]]|access-date=25 August 2026|date=9 July 2024|quote=Čančar missed the entirety of the 2023-24 season
